text:
arjun: Quick heads-up — I'm running a KV prefetcher sensitivity experiment. Goal: do an apples-to-apples comparison between our replay harness and synthetic-load generator to surface any hit-rate biasing or warmup differences. Planning to capture hit-rates, warmup time, eviction churn, and p95/p99 token latency.

maria: Nice. Can you spell out the exact harness params you want matched? seq-len dist, arrival process, kernel pinning etc.

arjun: Sure — current plan (will run each config under both replay and synthetic):
```
model: redwood/v1-7B
seq_len_dist: sample from eval_prompt_lengths.json (same seed across runs)
arrival: constant QPS 120 (10 clients x 12) + separate Poisson run
clients: 10
concurrency_per_gpu: 16
runtime flags: --kv-prefetch=on --prefetch-window=3 --kernel-policy=auto
metrics: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_hit_rate (per-step), eviction_ops/s, cpu%
duration: 10m (ignore first 60s as warmup)
```

ben: Add two baselines: 1) prefetch disabled, 2) aggressive prefetch (--prefetch-window=6). Also force kernel variants (fused vs vanilla) as a micro-experiment. Measure tail latency both with and without batching.

ciara: Preliminary numbers from the replay harness (10m, same seed) — very rough: baseline (prefetch off): warmup ~90s, steady-state kv_hit_rate ~58%, overall avg token/sec 115. default prefetch: warmup ~45s, steady kv_hit_rate ~74%, avg token/sec 132. aggressive prefetch: kv_hit_rate ~86% but p95 latency increases ~+8ms (likely contention on KV eviction path).

arjun: Interesting — the warmup halving is expected but the p95 regression with aggressive prefetch is concerning. Could be eviction thrashing under high concurrency. Did you capture eviction_ops/s and GC stalls?

ciara: Yep — eviction_ops/s jumped from ~120 -> ~420 for aggressive prefetch; CPU on the runtime host +18%. GC pause traces show a few 10-20ms stalls coincident with p95 spikes.

perf-bot: Artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.internal/bench/1782345678/prefetch-sensitivity-report.html (contains CSVs, flamegraphs, and kv-key-distribution histograms) :memo:

maria: To isolate whether kernel selection interacts with prefetching we should run the exact same trace while forcing kernel selection: `--kernel-policy=fused_attention` and `--kernel-policy=vanilla`. That will tell us if fused kernels cause different memory access patterns that amplify eviction. Example command: 
```bash
./run_bench --trace replay_trace.tar --qps 120 --concurrency 16 --runtime-flags "--kv-prefetch=on --prefetch-window=3 --kernel-policy=fused_attention"
```

ben: Also recommend a micro synthetic that single-threads the runtime (concurrency=1) while keeping the same arrival rates to see whether the issue is purely concurrency/locking. If single-thread removes p95 regression, it's likely lock/eviction contention.

arjun: Good calls. Next actions: ciara -> run synthetic Poisson arrival with seed=42 and prefetch-window {0,3,6}; ben -> prepare kernel-forced runs and a single-thread microbench; maria -> extract eviction logs + KV key freq histogram from artifacts and add them to the report. Aim: have numbers and a short write-up by EOD Friday. I'll collect and create a perf-regression ticket if we see a regression. :thumbsup:

ciara: Got it, will start the Poisson runs now and attach CSVs to the artifact when done.

ben: On it, will push kernel variants to the job template and share commands.

maria: I will add eviction histograms and a small note about normalization (always zero background traffic and identical seq_len seed).

arjun: Thanks all — flagging this for the perf working group. If anyone sees surprising diffs, drop logs here.
